newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dollars again to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dollars again to support won.

text.p: South Korea's central Bank of Korea (BOK) sold dollars again in afternoon trading to support the won as it tested six-year lows against the dollar, dealers said.
They said the BOK began selling dollars at the 829.30 level as soon as the afternoon session opened.
"The central bank's intention to support the won looks firm," said a dealer with a foreign bank
Dealers said the won was currently under pressure due to strong dollar demand for importer settlements.
"As the nation's exports have become sluggish, demand for the dollar is expected to remain strong," said a dealer with a domestic bank.

Dollar inflows for investment in the Seoul stock market fell sharply this week. About $550 million came in last week after the limit for foreign stock ownership was raised to 20 percent from 18 percent.
